answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering node representing a node within one particular layer network, rather than a layer-independent physical device.
answers.example: ROADM R1 as represented in the OTN layer.
answers.relations: It is part of i.tetopo. TE links i.telink run between TE nodes; termination points i.tp are on TE nodes and terminate those links. Connectivity constraints i.cmatrix and tunnel connection endpoints i.tcep may also be associated with a TE node.

answers.gloss: A termination point on a TE node at which a TE link terminates.
answers.example: The termination point on R1 facing R2 for the R1-R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It is owned by or located on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. A TP can participate in a cross-layer supporting relationship represented by i.stp.

answers.gloss: The supporting relationship by which a client-layer termination point is supported by a server-layer termination point; it represents cross-layer adaptation rather than an ordinary same-layer link.
answers.example: An OTN termination point at R1 supported by an optical-layer termination point at R1.
answers.relations: It relates termination points i.tp across client and server layers, with the server-layer TP supporting the client-layer TP. It is not itself a node-to-node TE link.

answers.gloss: The point at which a TE tunnel originates or terminates—a trail head associated with the tunnel endpoint node. It is a tunnel endpoint, not inherently an externally exposed service-access point.
answers.example: The A1 trail head of the A1-A3 ODU2 tunnel.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel. My model does not equate it with an external customer-facing interface, nor does it explicitly identify it with i.tcep.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel that realizes a service across the TE network.
answers.example: An ODU2 tunnel from A1 to A3.
answers.relations: It starts and ends at i.ttp, is routed over i.tetopo, may be labeled with i.otnlabel, and contains or is associated with tunnel connection endpoints i.tcep at nodes.

answers.gloss: An OTN technology-specific label expressing tributary-slot and tributary-port-number multiplexing information used to place a client ODU into a server OTN container.
answers.example: The TS/TPN selection for carrying an ODU2 in an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel. It identifies multiplexing allocation or structure, especially tributary slots, rather than denoting a topology object or endpoint by itself.

answers.gloss: A matrix of permitted internal connectivity within a TE node, describing which termination-side resources may be interconnected or switched through that node.
answers.example: R2's matrix permitting connectivity from its R1-facing TP to its R3-facing TP while disallowing some other TP pairings.
answers.relations: It is associated with i.tenode and constrains possible intra-node connectivity among termination points i.tp. It complements inter-node connectivity supplied by i.telink.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering link between TE nodes within one layer network.
answers.example: The R1-R2 TE link in the OTN layer.
answers.relations: It runs between i.tenode instances, is terminated by i.tp at its ends, and is contained in i.tetopo.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering network topology for a particular layer network. In this model, layers are represented as separate per-layer topologies rather than collapsed into one undifferentiated topology.
answers.example: The OTN layer network containing R1, R2, R3 and their OTN TE links.
answers.relations: It contains i.tenode and i.telink. The cross-layer supporting relationship i.stp relates resources of different per-layer representations, while i.tunnel is routed over the topology.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node, representing where that tunnel's connection is anchored or terminated at that node.
answers.example: The connection endpoint for the A1-A3 tunnel on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and is part of i.tunnel. The model does not state a direct identity or explicit relation between i.tcep and i.ttp: i.ttp is the tunnel's trail head, whereas i.tcep is a connection endpoint within a node.

answers.gloss: A forwarding node represented in the domain's single multi-layer topology.
answers.example: ROADM R1.
answers.relations: It is part of t.topo. Topological links t.link run between nodes; t.ltp, t.sip, t.nrg, and t.cep are located on nodes. Unlike i.tenode as described, t.node is not defined as belonging to only one particular layer topology.

answers.gloss: An edge point owned by a node where a topological link terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point facing R2.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and terminates t.link. The supplied model does not define direct t.ltp-to-t.cep or t.ltp-to-layer-protocol relations, nor does it characterize t.ltp as aggregating CEPs.

answers.gloss: A link object expressing adaptation between layers at a node.
answers.example: The OTU4-to-ODU2 adaptation at R1.
answers.relations: It is located at t.node and expresses an adaptation characterized by t.lpq. Its modeled instance is an adaptation link, not an ordinary node-to-node t.link. The supplied relations do not enumerate separate endpoint objects for its client and server sides.

answers.gloss: A point where an external client service accesses the network.
answers.example: The customer-facing ODU2 hand-off at A1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and provides access to t.cs. It is an externally exposed service-access abstraction, distinct in meaning from an internal connection endpoint such as t.cep.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end connectivity service across the network.
answers.example: The A1-to-A3 ODU2 service.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip as its service access points, is realized by t.cep, is carried over t.topo, and may be qualified by t.lpq. It denotes service connectivity; the model does not separately expose an engineered tunnel/path object.

answers.gloss: A qualifier expressing the multiplexing and layer structure of a signal.
answers.example: ODU2 mapped into an OTU4 server.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and characterizes the adaptation expressed by t.translink. It describes protocol/layer and multiplexing structure; the supplied model does not explicitly define it as a concrete tributary-slot or tributary-port allocation.

answers.gloss: A group of constraints governing which ports may be cross-connected within a node.
answers.example: The permitted internal cross-connects on R2.
answers.relations: It is associated with t.node and constrains intra-node switching. Although its semantics concern port cross-connectivity, the supplied relation list does not explicitly connect it to individual t.ltp or t.cep objects.

answers.gloss: A topological link between two nodes.
answers.example: The R1-R2 link.
answers.relations: It runs between t.node instances, is terminated by t.ltp at its ends, and is contained in t.topo.

answers.gloss: The single multi-layer topology describing the domain.
answers.example: The combined OTN-over-optical domain topology.
answers.relations: It contains t.node and t.link, and t.cs is provided over it. Unlike the disclosed i.tetopo, it may combine multiple layers in one topology rather than representing exactly one layer per topology.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a connection within a node.
answers.example: The connection endpoint for the A1-A3 service on R1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and is part of or realizes t.cs. It is an internal connection endpoint, distinct from the external service access represented by t.sip. The supplied model does not state direct relations from t.cep to t.ltp or t.sip.

proposals.rationale: Both denote node-owned edge termination points at which corresponding topological or TE links terminate, with matching endpoint identity and link relations.
Both encode permitted intra-node connectivity or cross-connect constraints among termination-side resources, complementing inter-node links.
Both denote inter-node topological links terminated by node-owned termination points and contained in a topology; the TE dialect adds a layer-specific framing.
Both are internal connection endpoints on nodes and belong to the corresponding end-to-end service or tunnel, as illustrated by the A1-A3 endpoint on R1.
